title: Eldercare is a large and uneven time institution
source_unit: ATUS respondent age 15+ in combined 2023-2024 published eldercare tables

observations.period: 2023-2024 combined; total civilian noninstitutional population age 15+
observations.method: BLS published 2023-2024 Unpaid Eldercare in the United States tables; provider means a person age 15+ who cared during the prior three to four months for someone age 65+ with an aging-related condition.
observations.uncertainty: Published-table estimate; no interval is reproduced in this record. Recall window, sample design, and combined-year estimation remain relevant limitations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Provider prevalence is not care intensity, a family-panel measure, or evidence that care displaced paid work or social participation.

hours_all_provider_days.unit: hours per day averaged across providers

observations.method: BLS published 2023-2024 Table 4; care-day hours are conditional on a diary day with eldercare, while the all-provider-day measure averages across providers.
observations.uncertainty: Published-table estimate; no interval is reproduced in this record. Diary-day selection and activity reporting limit displacement claims.
observations.counterinterpretation: Care on a diary day is not a counterfactual loss of work; providers may care on non-work days or outside reported work activities.

hours_all_provider_days.unit: hours per day averaged across providers

observations.method: BLS published 2023-2024 Table 4; care-day hours are conditional on a diary day with eldercare.
observations.uncertainty: Published-table estimate; no interval is reproduced in this record. Diary-day selection and activity reporting limit displacement claims.
observations.counterinterpretation: Full-time status and care-day hours do not establish schedule control, employer accommodation, or work reduction.

observations.method: BLS published 2023-2024 Tables 1 and 4; age-group population and provider measures are descriptive combined-year estimates.
observations.uncertainty: Published-table estimate; no interval is reproduced in this record. Provider definition and recall window do not measure a dated care event.
observations.counterinterpretation: A high provider rate in this age group does not show that care caused employment, health, or household changes.

observations.method: BLS published 2023-2024 Tables 1 and 4; age-group population and provider measures are descriptive combined-year estimates.
observations.uncertainty: Published-table estimate; no interval is reproduced in this record. Provider definition and recall window do not measure a dated care event.
observations.counterinterpretation: The older-provider pattern is not equivalent to retired-only care or to household-bound care; recipient relationship and support network matter.

household_activities_share.unit: percent of reported eldercare activity time

household_member_care_share.unit: percent of reported eldercare activity time

nonhousehold_member_care_share.unit: percent of reported eldercare activity time

observations.method: BLS published 2023-2024 Table 5; activity percentages describe reported care-day activities and are not a mutually exclusive allocation of all respondent time.
observations.uncertainty: Published-table estimate; activity overlap and diary-day selection prevent interpretation as a full time budget or displacement estimate.
observations.counterinterpretation: The low reported work-activity share on care days does not show that care caused work cessation; care may occur on non-work days or outside the measured activity.

boundary: This is an official combined-year published-table population layer. It measures eldercare prevalence and time on care days, not a same-family panel, a dated trigger, care-recipient outcome, counterfactual work displacement, schedule control, later wellbeing, trust, political action, or causal effect. The retrieval hash covers the committed analysis memo.
